mainTopic: Laws of מעשר שני: lashes for eating it outside the wall or in טומאה, when it may be redeemed, and when liability begins
overview: This עמוד is all about מעשר שני. First the גמרא finishes a question about learning a מעשר שני law from בכור through a היקש, and answers that the blood and meat of the בכור count as one thing. Next it explains that our משנה and the earlier one on 13a teach two different lashes: one for eating טהור מעשר שני outside the wall, and one for eating it in טומאה inside ירושלים. The גמרא then finds the source for the טומאה prohibition. It starts from רבי שמעון's ברייתא on 'לא בערתי ממנו בטמא' and finds the warning in 'לא תוכל לאכול בשעריך', read against the בכור. It then learns from the word 'שאתו' two laws: טמא מעשר שני may be redeemed even in ירושלים, and טהור מעשר שני may be redeemed even one step outside the wall. רב חנינא and רב הושעיא ask about a person inside the city whose load is outside, and the answer is 'ממילואך': the person and his load count together. רב פפא's question about a load on a reed stays תיקו. Finally רבי יוחנן teaches that lashes for eating מעשר שני outside apply only once it has entered the walls, and the גמרא begins a challenge from רבי יוסי's case of a כהן tithing one fig, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Does the derivation work for the view that follows the teaching source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether learning the מעשר שני law from בכור is allowed according to the view that we follow the 'teacher' in deciding whether a derivation counts as קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says we follow the thing being learned. But for the one who says we follow the thing doing the teaching, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the derivation it just made, where the law for מעשר שני was learned from בכור, which was itself learned from blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In קדשים, a law learned from a היקש cannot be used to teach another law through a היקש. If we judge by the 'learner', which is מעשר שני and counts as חולין for this rule, there is no problem. If we judge by the 'teacher', which is בכור and is קדשים, the two-step learning should not be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (setting up a 'but')
The thing being learned (the item that receives the law)
The thing doing the teaching (the source of the law)
We follow / we decide based on
What is there to say? (a challenge formula)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether מעשר שני is forbidden outside the wall. Everyone agrees it is. The question is only whether this particular way of learning it is allowed.

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says
we follow the thing that is learned
phrases.notes: Here that means מעשר שני, which is treated like חולין for this rule.

phrases.english: but according to the one who says
we follow the thing that teaches
phrases.notes: Here that means the בכור, which is a קרבן.

phrases.english: what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בָּתַר לָמֵד אָזְלִינַן, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בָּתַר מְלַמֵּד אָזְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the היקש derivation made just before this point in the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: Learning מעשר שני from בכור, when בכור itself was learned from blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the teacher decides the rule, the teacher here is קדשים. In קדשים, something learned from a היקש cannot teach again through a היקש.

steps.title: Blood and meat count as one thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the blood and the meat of the בכור are one single matter, so there is only one היקש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Blood and meat are one thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying there was never a two-step learning chain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בכור's meat was not 'learned' from its blood in a separate step, because blood and meat are one unit. So מעשר שני is learned directly from the blood-and-meat of the בכור in a single היקש. That is allowed even under the view that follows the teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood and meat (of the קרבן)
One single matter

steps.whatToRemember: There is no problem of a law learned from a היקש teaching again in קדשים, because the blood and meat of the בכור are one matter.

phrases.english: Blood and meat are one matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case so there is only one derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the meat of the בכור was learned from its blood, which would make two steps of learning.
steps.terutzMaskana: Blood and meat are one unit, so there is one direct היקש and it is allowed.

steps.title: Why does the משנה repeat the law of מעשר שני?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes our משנה and asks why it teaches lashes for eating מעשר שני when an earlier משנה already taught this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'קדשי קדשים, etc.' But we already learned this once: 'מעשר שני and הקדש that were not redeemed!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new line of our משנה and points out what looks like a repeat of an earlier משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה lists eating מעשר שני outside the wall among the cases that get lashes. An earlier משנה already listed eating מעשר שני that was not redeemed. A משנה should not teach the same law twice, so something must be different between the two.

keyTerms.meaning: The most holy קרבנות (such as עולה and חטאת)
One time
Property dedicated to the בית המקדש
Were redeemed (exchanged for money)

phrases.english: Most holy offerings, etc.
We already learned this one time
second tithe and consecrated property that were not redeemed!
phrases.notes: This line comes from an earlier משנה, on 13a.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on the next line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The mention of מעשר שני in our משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same law seems to be taught twice, which a משנה should not do.

steps.title: The two משניות deal with different cases
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא explains that our משנה is about eating טהור מעשר שני outside the wall. The earlier משנה is about eating טמא מעשר שני while טמא, inside ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: The later משנה is about pure מעשר שני and a pure man who eats it outside the wall. The earlier משנה is about impure מעשר שני and an impure man who eats it in ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר חנינא answers the question by showing that the two משניות teach two separate laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה gives lashes for eating in the wrong place, outside the wall. The earlier משנה gives lashes for eating in the wrong state, in טומאה, even inside ירושלים. Since these are two different prohibitions, there is no repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: The later clause (here, our משנה)
The earlier clause (here, the earlier משנה)
The man / the person
Outside the wall (of ירושלים)
Ritually impure / ritually pure

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that eating מעשר שני in טומאה is its own prohibition with lashes. That leads straight into the next question about where it comes from.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said
The latter clause is about pure second tithe
phrases.notes: 'The latter clause' here means our משנה, which comes later than the one on 13a.

phrases.english: and a pure man
who eats it outside the wall.
The first clause is about impure second tithe
and an impure man
and he eats it in Jerusalem.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא: סֵיפָא בְּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the repetition question in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two משניות into different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought both משניות were about the same prohibition of eating מעשר שני.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה is about eating outside the wall. The earlier one is about eating in טומאה inside ירושלים.

steps.title: What is the source for lashes for eating in טומאה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that a person gets lashes for eating מעשר שני in טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that one is liable for it because of טומאה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the law that רבי יוסי בר חנינא just used. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי בר חנינא's answer depends on there being lashes for eating מעשר שני in טומאה. The גמרא now wants to see where that prohibition comes from in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
Is liable (here, for lashes)
Ritual impurity

phrases.english: And from where do we know that one is liable for it
because of impurity?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the law that step 4 relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The תורה source for the prohibition, with lashes, of eating מעשר שני in טומאה

steps.title: רבי שמעון reads the פסוק as covering both kinds of טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי שמעון learns from 'לא בערתי ממנו בטמא' that מעשר שני may not be used in טומאה, whether the person is טמא or the food is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי שמעון says: 'I have not removed any of it while impure' means whether I am impure and it is pure, or I am pure and it is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא that reads the פסוק from וידוי מעשר as banning מעשר שני in טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says only 'בטמא' and does not say who is טמא. So רבי שמעון reads it broadly to include both a טמא person and טמא food. This fits the earlier משנה's case of a טמא person eating טמא מעשר שני.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I have not removed any of it while impure' (דברים 26:14)
Whether... or whether

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Shimon says
"I have not removed any of it while impure"
phrases.notes: דברים 26:14

phrases.english: whether I am impure and it is pure
or whether I am pure and it is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source asked for in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'לא בערתי ממנו בטמא' bans מעשר שני in טומאה, whether the person or the food is טמא.

steps.title: רבי שמעון does not know the warning against eating
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון adds that he does not know where the תורה gives the actual warning, the אזהרה, against eating מעשר שני in טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But where one is warned about eating, I do not know.
steps.whatsHappening: Still in the ברייתא, רבי שמעון points out a gap. The פסוק shows the act is wrong, but it is not a clear warning against eating. This sets up the גמרא's next search for that warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lashes need a clear negative warning, an אזהרה. 'לא בערתי' is a declaration the farmer makes, not a direct command. So at this point the source for lashes is still missing. Steps 8-10 find it.

keyTerms.meaning: Warned (given a negative commandment)
Eating
I do not know

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not saying eating in טומאה is allowed. He knows it is forbidden. He only does not know which פסוק gives the warning against it.

phrases.english: But where is one warned about eating
I do not know.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵיכָן מוּזְהָר עַל אֲכִילָה אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the source in step 6 is not enough by itself to give lashes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק gives the actual warning (אזהרה) against eating מעשר שני in טומאה

steps.title: Narrowing רבי שמעון's question to food that is itself טמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that a טמא person eating holy food is already covered by a clear פסוק. So רבי שמעון must be asking about food that is itself טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a person who is טמא, a פסוק says it openly: 'A person who touches it shall be טמא until evening and shall not eat of the holy foods.' Rather, his question is this: where do we learn the warning when the food itself is טמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבי שמעון really meant when he said he could not find the warning. It narrows his question to one case: מעשר שני food that has itself become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of טומאה: the person is טמא, or the food is טמא. A person who is טמא already has an open warning in ויקרא 22:6. So רבי שמעון's doubt must be about the food's own טומאה, and that is now the question to answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The person's own body is ritually impure
The food itself is ritually impure
Openly, stated in so many words
Holy foods; here this includes מעשר שני

steps.confusionAlert: 'עצמו' does not mean the person himself. It means the food itself. The person's טומאה is the 'גוף' case, and that one is already solved.

phrases.english: Impurity of the body: it is written openly:
"A person who touches it
shall be impure until the evening
and shall not eat of the holy foods, etc."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:6. The holy foods here include מעשר שני.

phrases.english: Rather: the impurity of itself, from where?
phrases.notes: 'Itself' means the food: where's the warning when the מעשר שני food itself is the thing that's טמא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what רבי שמעון's open question in step 7 is really about
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of the warning against eating מעשר שני when the food itself is טמא

steps.title: Two 'within your gates' פסוקים are set side by side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by placing the מעשר שני פסוק 'you may not eat within your gates' next to the בכור פסוק 'within your gates you shall eat it, the טמא and the טהור'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'You may not eat within your gates.' And further on it says: 'Within your gates you shall eat it, the impure and the pure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by pairing two פסוקים that both use the words 'within your gates'. This sets up the next step, where it explains how the pairing works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק is about מעשר שני and forbids eating it 'within your gates'. The second is about a blemished בכור and allows it 'within your gates' for the טמא and the טהור. The shared words hint that the מעשר שני prohibition is aimed at the very leniency the בכור is given.

keyTerms.meaning: Within your gates, meaning in your own towns
And further on, in another place in the תורה
The impure and the pure

phrases.english: As it is written: "You may not eat within your gates."
phrases.notes: דברים 12:17, said about מעשר שני.

phrases.english: And further on it says:
"Within your gates you shall eat it,
the impure and the pure,"
phrases.notes: דברים 15:22, said about a בכור animal that has a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question asked in step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The warning comes from reading 'לא תוכל לאכול בשעריך' together with the בכור פסוק 'בשעריך תאכלנו הטמא והטהור'

steps.title: What is allowed for the בכור is forbidden for מעשר שני
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא of דבי רבי ישמעאל teaches that the בכור may be eaten even when the meat is טמא. So the תורה is saying that this leniency does not apply to מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: even a טמא person and a טהור person may eat from one dish, and they need not worry. So the תורה is saying: that טמא food which I allowed you to eat alongside the טהור there, you may not eat here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that the בכור is allowed even when the meat itself is טמא. Then it finishes the answer: מעשר שני does not get that leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a טמא person and a טהור person share one dish, the meat becomes טמא, and the טהור person still eats it. That shows the בכור may be eaten even when the food is טמא. 'You may not eat' about מעשר שני therefore forbids exactly this, so it is the warning against eating מעשר שני that is itself טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: One dish, shared by both people
And they need not be concerned
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
There (the בכור) / here (מעשר שני)

steps.whatToRemember: The warning against eating טמא מעשר שני comes from 'לא תוכל לאכול בשעריך'. It forbids for מעשר שני the leniency the תורה gives the blemished בכור, which may be eaten even when it is טמא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finds the missing warning רבי שמעון was looking for. That warning is the basis for giving lashes for eating מעשר שני that is itself טמא.

phrases.english: And the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Even an impure person and a pure person
may eat from one dish
and they need not be concerned.
phrases.notes: The טמא person makes the shared meat טמא, and the טהור person may still eat it.

phrases.english: And the Merciful One is saying:
That impure food which is permitted to you
together with the pure there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the בכור.

phrases.english: here you may not eat.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means מעשר שני.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from step 9 by showing how the two פסוקים connect
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מעשר שני may not be eaten in the way the בכור may, when the food is טמא; this is the warning
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of דבי רבי ישמעאל, which allows sharing one dish

steps.title: How do we know טמא מעשר שני can be redeemed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new question: what is the source that טמא מעשר שני can be redeemed?
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that it is something that can be redeemed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. Earlier it said the משנה's case of unredeemed מעשר שני is about טמא produce, which assumes such produce can be redeemed. Now it asks where we learn that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling טמא מעשר שני 'not redeemed' only makes sense if it is able to be redeemed. The גמרא wants a source for that. The next step gives the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Redemption: moving the holiness of מעשר שני onto money
Something that is able to be redeemed
And from where do we know

phrases.english: And from where do we know
that it is something that can be redeemed?
phrases.notes: 'It' is מעשר שני that became טמא, the case of the earlier משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the warning topic and asks about an assumption behind the answer in step 4
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that טמא מעשר שני can be redeemed

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's source: 'carry' means 'eat'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר derives from 'כי לא תוכל שאתו' that טמא מעשר שני may be redeemed even in ירושלים, because שאת can mean eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אלעזר said: How do we know that מעשר שני that became טמא may be redeemed even in ירושלים? The פסוק says 'because you cannot שְׂאֵתוֹ (carry it).' And 'שאת' means eating, as it says 'he carried portions (משאת) from before him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 11 by quoting רבי אלעזר. He reads the פסוק's word 'carry it' as 'eat it', so if you can't eat the produce because it is טמא, you may redeem it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to talk about produce that is too far away to carry to ירושלים. רבי אלעזר shows that the same root (נשא) is used for food portions in בראשית, so 'you cannot שאתו' also means 'you cannot eat it'. Food that is טמא can't be eaten, so it may be redeemed even inside ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe: produce that must be eaten in ירושלים, or redeemed for money
We redeem, meaning we transfer its holiness onto money
Literally 'to carry it'; here read as 'to eat it'
Eating
Portions or gifts of food

steps.whyThisMatters: The same word, שאתו, will be used again in the next steps, which sets up a question of whether one word can teach two laws.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Elazar said:
From where do we know regarding second tithe that became impure
that we may redeem it even in Jerusalem?
The verse says: 'Because you are unable to carry it.'
phrases.notes: דברים 14:24

phrases.english: And 'carrying' means nothing other than eating,
as it is said: 'And he carried portions from before him.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 43:34. These 'portions' were food that יוסף sent to his brothers.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מִנַּיִן לְמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁנִּטְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11's question about where we learn that טמא מעשר שני can be redeemed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'כי לא תוכל שאתו', reading שאת as eating. טמא produce can't be eaten, so it may be redeemed even in ירושלים.

steps.title: Pure tithe may be redeemed one step outside the wall
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי in the name of רב אסי derives from the same פסוק that טהור מעשר שני may be redeemed even one step outside ירושלים's wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי said in the name of רב אסי: How do we know that טהור מעשר שני may be redeemed even one step outside the wall? Because it says 'because you cannot carry it.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching uses the same words, 'you cannot carry it'. It teaches that pure produce may be redeemed even when it is just outside the wall, not only when it is far away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק also mentions the place being 'too far from you'. רב אסי reads 'you cannot carry it' as its own reason: if for any reason you can't bring it in, you may redeem it, even if it is very close to the city.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritually pure
One step
Outside the wall of ירושלים

steps.confusionAlert: Here the produce is טהור and outside the city. In step 12 it was טמא and inside the city. These are two different cases.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rav Beivai said in the name of Rav Asi:
From where do we know regarding pure second tithe
that we may redeem it even
one step outside the wall?
As it is said: 'Because you are unable to carry it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי אָמַר רַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related teaching that uses the same word from the פסוק as step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pure מעשר שני may be redeemed even one step outside ירושלים's wall.

steps.title: That verse is already used for רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that שאתו is already needed for רבי אלעזר's teaching about טמא produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this פסוק is needed for רבי אלעזר's teaching!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אסי. The word שאתו is already being used by רבי אלעזר, so how can רב אסי use it too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that one word normally teaches one law. If שאתו means 'eat' for רבי אלעזר, it seems it can't also teach about pure produce outside the wall.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for, meaning it is already used for another teaching

phrases.english: This is needed for the teaching of Rabbi Elazar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 13's use of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word שאתו is already used up by רבי אלעזר's teaching.

steps.title: If only eating was meant, the תורה would say 'eat'
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק only meant eating, it would have said 'לאוכלו'. Choosing שאתו shows an extra teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the פסוק say 'you cannot eat it'. Why does it say 'carry it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אסי. If the תורה only wanted to teach about eating, it would have used the plain word for 'eat'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The unusual word שאתו shows that the תורה also means real carrying. That is where רב אסי's teaching about pure produce comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let the פסוק say, meaning the תורה could have written it differently
To eat it

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say
'You are unable to eat it,'
Why does it say 'carry it'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, לֵימָא קְרָא ״לֹא תוּכַל לְאוֹכְלוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra meaning from an unusual word choice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שאתו only teaches about eating טמא produce.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the תורה wrote 'carry' instead of 'eat', it also teaches about carrying.

steps.title: Maybe the word is only about carrying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes from the other side: maybe שאתו teaches only רב אסי's law and nothing about טמא produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that the whole word comes only for this teaching!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's side. Maybe the word means only carrying, and teaches nothing about eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שאתו simply means 'carry', the plain reading supports רב אסי alone. Then רבי אלעזר would be left with no source.

keyTerms.meaning: But say, a suggestion of a different reading
It all comes only for this purpose

phrases.english: But say it comes entirely for this purpose!
phrases.notes: 'This purpose' means רב אסי's teaching about pure produce just outside the wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 15 from the opposite direction.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's reading of שאתו as eating
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Maybe the word means only physical carrying, which leaves no source for טמא produce.

steps.title: If only carrying was meant, the תורה would say 'take'
steps.stepSummary: If only carrying was meant, the תורה would have said 'ליטלו'. Choosing שאתו points to eating as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the פסוק say 'you cannot take it'. Why does it say שאתו?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אלעזר. If the תורה only meant carrying, it would have used a plain word like 'take'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה picked שאתו, a word that is also used for food portions. That choice hints at eating, so רבי אלעזר's teaching stands.

keyTerms.meaning: To take it

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say
'You are unable to take it,'
Why does it say 'carry it'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, לֵימָא קְרָא ״לֹא תוּכַל לִיטְּלוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra meaning from an unusual word choice
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the תורה wrote שאתו instead of 'take', it also hints at eating.

steps.title: The word teaches both laws
steps.stepSummary: Conclusion: שאתו teaches both רבי אלעזר's law and רב אסי's law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the one word teaches two laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither 'eat' nor 'take' alone was written. The תורה's choice of שאתו covers both meanings. So טמא produce may be redeemed inside ירושלים, and טהור produce may be redeemed right outside the wall.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn two things from it

steps.whatToRemember: שאתו has two meanings. 'Eat' means טמא מעשר שני may be redeemed even in ירושלים. 'Carry' means טהור מעשר שני may be redeemed even one step outside the wall.

phrases.english: Conclude two things from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the back-and-forth from steps 14 to 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both teachings come from the word שאתו.

steps.title: What about produce at the entrance of Jerusalem?
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא and רב הושעיא ask about the law of מעשר שני located right at the entrance of ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא and רב הושעיא were sitting, and they asked: what is the law at the entrance of ירושלים?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is raised about produce right at the city's entrance. The גמרא is setting up a question that the next line will explain more exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that one step outside the wall is still 'outside' and the produce may be redeemed there. Now the question is about the exact border: does the entrance count as inside or outside?

keyTerms.meaning: They had a question
Entrance, gateway
What is the law?

phrases.english: Rav Chanina and Rav Hoshaya were sitting,
and they had a question:
At the entrance of Jerusalem, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב חֲנִינָא וְרַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא, וְקָא מִבַּעְיָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the topic of where redemption may happen, at the very edge of the city.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether produce at the entrance counts as inside ירושלים.

steps.title: Person inside, produce outside
steps.stepSummary: If the person is outside and his load is inside, the walls clearly take it in. The real question is when the person is inside and his load is outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that if he is outside and his load is inside, the walls have taken it in. But if he is inside and his load is outside, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the question. It says which case is simple and which case is the real doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce that is physically inside the walls counts as inside, wherever its owner stands. The doubt is when the produce itself is outside but its owner is inside. Maybe the owner's position pulls the produce in.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
His load, the produce he is carrying
The walls have 'taken it in', so it now counts as inside

phrases.english: It is obvious: if he is outside and his load is inside,
the walls have taken it in,
if he is inside and his load is outside, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the exact case the question in step 19 is about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether produce outside the wall counts as inside when its owner is standing inside.

steps.title: From your fullness: the load counts as part of the person
steps.stepSummary: An elder quotes the school of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: 'ממך' in the פסוק is read as 'ממילואך', you and everything you carry. If any part of the person or his load is inside, he counts as inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain elder taught them a teaching from the school of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: 'If the place is too far from you (ממך)' means 'from your fullness (ממילואך)'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 20, about a person inside the city whose load is outside. It quotes an old teaching that treats the person and his load as one unit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה allows redeeming מעשר שני when 'the place is too far from you'. Reading 'ממך' as 'ממילואך' means 'you' includes your whole package: your body plus whatever you carry. So if the person is inside the walls, his load counts as inside too, and he may no longer redeem it.

keyTerms.meaning: An elder; here an older scholar who reported a teaching
The school of; the study house of a certain sage
From you
From your fullness: you together with everything you carry

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that a person and the load he carries are judged together when deciding whether he is inside ירושלים.

phrases.english: A certain elder taught them
a teaching of the school of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
"If the place is too far from you"
phrases.notes: דברים 14:24

phrases.english: means: from your fullness.
phrases.notes: The word 'from you' is read as 'from your fullness', meaning you plus everything you're carrying.

steps.triggerLanguage: תנא להו ההוא סבא בדבי רבי שמעון בן יוחי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the narrowed question of Step 20 (person inside, load outside).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a person inside the walls whose load is outside may still redeem the מעשר שני.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. 'ממך' means 'ממילואך', so the person and his load are one unit, and he counts as inside.

steps.title: What if the load hangs from a reed?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks: if the person holds the produce on a reed or pole instead of carrying it on his body, does it still count as his 'fullness'?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: if he holds it on a reed, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא tests the edge of the 'ממילואך' rule just learned. He asks about produce the person holds on a pole rather than on his body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'fullness' rule clearly covers a load resting on the person. A load hanging from a reed is held by him but not on him. The question is whether holding is enough to make it part of his 'fullness'.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked; he raised a question he was unsure about
Holding
A reed or pole

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
If he holds it on a reed, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the limits of the 'ממילואך' rule from Step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether produce held on a reed counts as part of the person's 'fullness'.

steps.title: The question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends רב פפא's question with תיקו: it stays unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds no answer to רב פפא's question and leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means the question stands without a decision. We do not know whether a load on a reed counts as part of the person.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: A load on the person counts as part of him (ממילואך). A load hanging from a reed is an open question (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of Step 22 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether a load held on a reed counts as part of the person remains undecided.

steps.title: Liability for eating מעשר שני outside starts once it enters the walls
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי quotes רבי יוחנן: one becomes liable for eating מעשר שני outside ירושלים only after the produce has 'seen the face of the wall', meaning it was brought inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: From when is one liable for eating מעשר שני outside ירושלים? From when it has seen the face of the wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: the point at which eating מעשר שני outside ירושלים becomes punishable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the produce ever enters ירושלים, eating it outside is not punished with מלקות. Once it has been brought inside the walls, taking it out and eating it outside does bring liability.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe, which must be eaten in ירושלים
From when?
Liable; here, to receive מלקות
The face of the wall; being brought inside the walls of ירושלים

steps.confusionAlert: 'Seen the face of the wall' does not mean the produce was just near the wall or in sight of it. It means the produce was brought inside the walls.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Second tithe: from when is one liable for it?
phrases.notes: He means liable to מלקות for eating it outside ירושלים.

phrases.english: From when it has seen the face of the wall.
phrases.notes: Meaning once the produce has been brought inside the walls.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי אסי אמר רבי יוחנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new related topic about מעשר שני and the walls of ירושלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability for eating מעשר שני outside ירושלים begins only after the produce has entered the walls.

steps.title: The source: the two neighboring פסוקים go together
steps.stepSummary: The reason comes from linking 'לפני ה׳ אלהיך תאכלנו' with 'לא תוכל לאכל בשעריך'. The ban on eating outside applies only where the produce has already reached the place of 'before ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? The פסוק says 'Before ה׳ your God you shall eat it', and it is written 'You may not eat within your gates'. Wherever 'Before ה׳ your God you shall eat it' applies, 'You may not eat within your gates' applies. Wherever 'Before ה׳ your God you shall eat it' does not apply, 'You may not eat within your gates' does not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the תורה source for רבי יוחנן's rule by pairing two פסוקים that sit next to each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition 'you may not eat within your gates' is tied to the positive command 'before ה׳ you shall eat it'. Only produce that has reached ירושלים, where 'before ה׳' applies, falls under the prohibition. Produce that never entered is not yet covered, so eating it outside brings no מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
The פסוק
Within your gates; in your own towns outside ירושלים
We read regarding it; the פסוק applies to it

steps.whatToRemember: The prohibition of eating מעשר שני outside ירושלים applies only to produce that has already entered the walls, because it is linked to 'לפני ה׳ אלהיך תאכלנו'.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because the verse says
"Before ה׳ your God you shall eat it (year by year)",
phrases.notes: דברים 12:18. Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.english: and it is written "(For) you may not eat within your gates",
phrases.notes: דברים 12:17. Here too, some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: wherever we read regarding it
"Before ה׳ your God you shall eat it"
we read regarding it
"You may not eat within your gates."
And wherever we do not read regarding it
"Before ה׳ your God you shall eat it"
we do not read regarding it
"You may not eat within your gates."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the תורה source for רבי יוחנן's rule in Step 24.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that liability starts only once the produce enters the walls.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The pairing of דברים 12:18 ('לפני ה׳ אלהיך תאכלנו') with דברים 12:17 ('לא תוכל לאכל בשעריך').

steps.title: A challenge begins: the כהן who tithes a single fig
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a challenge from רבי יוסי: a כהן designates תרומה, מעשר ראשון and מעשר שני (or מעשר עני) in different parts of one טבל fig, then eats it. The ruling and the challenge continue on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from רבי יוסי: A כהן who got hold of a fig of טבל says: 'This fig, its תרומה is at its stem, its מעשר ראשון is at its north side, and its מעשר שני is at its south side.' This is when it is a year of מעשר שני and he is in ירושלים, or a year of מעשר עני and he is outside ירושלים. If he ate it...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to רבי יוחנן by bringing a case from רבי יוסי. The sentence is cut off here, and the ruling that creates the difficulty comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן separates all the required portions inside one fig just by naming spots on it. In a מעשר שני year he does this while in ירושלים, so the מעשר שני portion becomes holy right there inside the walls. The ruling about eating the fig, which will press on רבי יוחנן's rule, is still to come.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which תרומה and tithes have not yet been separated
The portion given to a כהן
Its stem
First tithe, given to a לוי
Poor man's tithe, given in the third and sixth years
Areas outside ירושלים

phrases.english: They challenged: Rabbi Yosei says:
A kohen who came into possession of
a fig of untithed produce,
says: This fig,
its terumah is at its stem,
first tithe at its north side,
and second tithe at its south side.
And it is a year of second tithe
and he is in Jerusalem,
or a year of poor man's tithe
and he is outside Jerusalem,
if he ate it:
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next עמוד, where the ruling comes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge from a ברייתא against רבי יוחנן's rule in Steps 24-25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that liability for eating מעשר שני outside begins once it has entered the walls.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The setup is still in progress. The case involves מעשר שני designated inside ירושלים, and the ruling about eating the fig, which will create the difficulty, appears on the next עמוד.
